text:
Andrei Kuzmenko is on his fifth NHL team in four seasons: Vancouver, Calgary, Philadelphia, Los Angeles and now Pittsburgh. The Hockey Beast ran an "everything you need to know" piece this week, which tells you he's still a puzzle people are trying to solve. One assist in 11 games won't settle it.

The numbers aren't kind. He has no goals on 1.36 expected, his points rate is 0.43 per 60 minutes, and Pittsburgh takes only 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, nine points worse than without him. His ice time is down two minutes over his last ten, and he hasn't played since Nov. 3.

There's a reason teams keep trying. He scored 53 points in 45 KHL games for SKA St. Petersburg before coming over, which our league translation reads as about 70 over 82 NHL games, and he scored 39 goals in his first Vancouver season (a well-known high point). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last year credits him with clean exits. But his skating is in the 8th percentile for top speed. We project 10 goals if he plays. The question now is whether he gets back in the lineup.
headline: Kuzmenko's search for a fit
